stem.en: Kabir brushes his teeth and asks why plaque "comes back by morning if brushing kills the bacteria". What does brushing actually do?

text.en: It scrapes the biofilm off and scatters the cells, dropping their count below threshold. Survivors on the surface start leaking signal again, and in a still mouth overnight they reach threshold and rebuild. Brushing resets the count; it does not sterilise.
It kills them all and new ones arrive from food.

feedback.en: Brushing kills few. It disperses. The same bacteria rebuild.

text.en: It removes the sugar they eat.

feedback.en: Sugar feeds them, and less helps, but plaque forms even in a mouth that fasts overnight. The rebuild is a quorum reached again.
A film that is scattered every twelve hours never gets thick or old enough to do much damage. That is the point of the routine.

explanation.en: A biofilm is a threshold crossed. Brushing pushes the count back below it. Time in a still mouth pushes it back over.
